_note: Only states with a statewide just-cause statute are listed. rule carries the controlling citation inline.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

CA.rule: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (AB 1482, covers 12+ month tenancies; no-fault grounds require 1 month's rent relocation under § 1946.2(d); single-family/condo and housing under 15 years old are exempt); paired rent cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (CPI plus 5%, with a 10% absolute annual cap; sunsets Jan 1, 2030)

CO.rule: C.R.S. § 38-12-1303 (HB24-1098, eff. 2024-04-19; for-cause eviction required, with enumerated no-fault grounds; owner-occupied and short-term-rental premises are carved out)

DC.rule: D.C. Code § 42-3505.01 (Rental Housing Act of 1985; enumerated grounds + extensive notice/relocation rules)

ME.rule: 14 M.R.S. § 6002 (30-day notice required; rolling 12-month presumption of retaliation for tenant-organizing or code-complaint)

NH.rule: N.H. Rev. Stat. § 540:2 (10 enumerated grounds for restricted properties; no-fault permitted with proper notice for non-restricted)

NY.rule: NY Real Property Law art. 6-A, §§ 210-218 (Good Cause Eviction Law, L. 2024; mandatory in NYC per § 212, opt-in for localities outside NYC per § 213; small-landlord and high-rent units exempt)

OR.rule: ORS 90.427 (SB 608, statewide just-cause + 7%+CPI rent cap; 90-day notice + relocation for no-fault termination after first year)

VT.rule: 9 V.S.A. § 4467 (notice required; no-cause termination permitted only after first year of tenancy with 60/90-day notice)

WA.rule: RCW 59.18.650 (HB 1236, just-cause for periodic tenancies after first 12 months)
